dhp383:1: Cleave the stream boldly, drive away lusts, O Brahman.
dhp383:3: Knowing the destruction of the Elements of Being, you shall know the Uncreate, O Brahman.
dhp384:1: When a Brahman has crossed to the farther shore of Two States,
dhp384:3: Then all the fetters fall away from him, for then he knows.
dhp385:1: That man for whom exists neither the far shore nor the near shore, nor both the far and the near shore,
dhp385:3: That man who is fearless and free, that man I call a Brahman.
dhp386:1: He that meditates, he that is incorrupt,
dhp386:2: He that has done his duty, he that is free from the evil passions,
dhp386:3: He that has reached the supreme goal, that man I call a Brahman.
dhp387:1: By day shines the sun, by night gleams the moon,
dhp387:3: The Warrior shines in his armor, the Brahman shines in trance,
dhp387:5: But all the day and all the night the Buddha shines in splendor.
dhp388:1: Because a man has put away evil, therefore is he called a Brahman;
dhp388:2: Because he walks in righteousness, therefore is he called a monk;
dhp388:3: Because he has banished his own impurities, therefore is he called a monk.
dhp389:1: No one should strike at a Brahman, nor should a Brahman let fly at his assailant.
dhp389:3: Woe be to him that strikes a Brahman! Woe be to that Brahman who lets fly at his assailant!
dhp390:1: It is no small advantage to a Brahman if he restrain his mind from things that are dear to him;
dhp390:3: As fast as the intent to injure declines, so fast indeed does suffering subside.
dhp391:1: He that offends not by act or speech or thought,
dhp391:3: He that controls himself in these three respects, that man I call a Brahman.
dhp392:1: That man from whom one learns the Law preached by the Supremely Enlightened,
dhp392:3: That man should one reverence profoundly, even as a Brahman reverences the sacrificial fire.
dhp393:1: It is not matted locks or lineage or birth that makes a Brahman;
dhp393:3: But he in whom Truth exists, and the Law, he is blessed, he is a Brahman.
dhp394:1: What is the use of your matted locks, vain man? What is the use of your antelope skin?
dhp394:3: There is a jungle within you; it is only the exterior that you polish and cleanse.
dhp395:1: That man who wears refuse-rags, that man who is lean, that man whose veins stand out all over his body,
dhp395:3: That man who meditates alone in the forest, that man I call a Brahman.
dhp396:1: I call not a man a Brahman for that he has issued from the womb of a Brahman mother or sprung from a Brahman mother.
dhp396:3: Such a man addresses me as “Sir,” such a man has worldly possessions.
dhp396:5: But he that is without worldly possessions, he that seeks not the things of this world, him alone I call a Brahman.
dhp397:1: He that has severed all the attachments, he that trembles not,
dhp397:3: He that has escaped from every bond and is unshackled, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp398:1: He that has cut the strap, the thong, the rope, and all their appendages,
dhp398:3: He that has raised the cross-bar, he that is awakened, him I call a Brahman.
dhp399:1: He that endures abuse and stripes and bonds without offense,
dhp399:3: He whose power is patience and whose army is power, him I call a Brahman.
dhp400:1: He that is free from anger, he that performs his duties faithfully,
dhp400:2: He that keeps the Precepts, he that is free from lust,
dhp400:3: He that has subdued himself, he that wears his last body, him I call a Brahman.
dhp401:1: Even as water does not cling to a lotus-leaf, nor a grain of mustard-seed to the point of an awl,
dhp401:3: Whoso in like manner clings not to the pleasures of sense, him I call a Brahman.
dhp402:1: He that realizes right here in this world how his suffering may be ended,
dhp402:3: He whose burden has fallen from him, he who has freed himself from the shackles, him I call a Brahman.
dhp403:1: He that possesses profound wisdom, he that possesses intelligence,
dhp403:2: He that knows what is the Path and what is not the Path,
dhp403:3: He that has reached the supreme goal, him I call a Brahman.
dhp404:1: He that holds himself aloof both from householders and from the houseless,
dhp404:3: He that wanders about without a home, he that desires but little, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp405:1: He that has laid aside the rod, and inflicts not punishment on living beings, whether animate or inanimate,
dhp405:3: He that kills not nor causes to kill, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp406:1: He that opposes not those by whom he is opposed, he that is meek among those that have taken the rod,
dhp406:3: He that is free from craving among those that crave, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp407:1: That man from whom lust and hatred and pride and envy have been made to fall,
dhp407:3: Even as a grain of mustard-seed from the point of an awl, that man I call a Brahman.
dhp408:1: Free from harshness, instructing the hearer, truthful: such are the words a man should utter;
dhp408:3: Thereby he will offend none. Whoso thus speaks, him I call a Brahman.
dhp409:1: Whosoever here in this world takes nothing that is not given to him,
dhp409:3: Whether it be long or short, coarse or fine, beautiful or ugly, him I call a Brahman.
dhp410:1: He that has no desires, either in this world or in the next,
dhp410:3: He that is free from desires and free from fetters, him I call a Brahman.
dhp411:1: He that has no longings, he that fully understands, he that entertains no doubts,
dhp411:3: He that has plunged into the Deathless, him I call a Brahman.
dhp412:1: Whosoever in this world has escaped from the bonds both of good and of evil,
dhp412:3: Whosoever is free from sorrow, free from defilement, free from impurity, him I call a Brahman.
dhp413:1: He that is spotless as the moon, pure, serene, and clear,
dhp413:3: He in whom the essence of joy is extinct, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp414:1: Whoever has crossed this quagmire, difficult to cross, rebirth, delusion;
dhp414:2: Whoever has crossed and gained the other side;
dhp414:4: Whoever is devoted to meditation, free from lust, free from doubt,
dhp414:5: Free from Craving, tranquil, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp415:1: Whoever in this world renounces lusts, whoever abandons the house-life and retires from the world,
dhp415:3: Whoever has extinguished the essence of lust, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp416:1: Whoever in this world has abandoned Craving,
dhp416:4: Whoever has gone forth from the household life to the houseless life,
dhp416:6: Whoever has destroyed the essence of Craving, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp417:1: He that has cast off the bondage of things of earth,
dhp417:3: He that has thrown off every bond, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp418:1: He that has cast aside both pleasure and pain, he that is cold, free from passion,
dhp418:3: He that, strenuous, has overcome all the worlds, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp419:1: He that knows the passing away and rebirth of beings everywhere,
dhp419:3: He that is free from attachment, happy, and enlightened, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp420:1: He whose future estate is not known to gods or Gandhabbas or men,
dhp420:3: He who has destroyed the evil passions and has attained Arahatship, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp421:1: He that possesses naught in the present, the past, and the future,
dhp421:3: He that neither possesses aught nor yearns for aught, such a man I call a Brahman.
dhp422:1: The noble, the eminent, the manly, the wise, the conqueror,
dhp422:3: The pure, the sinless, the enlightened, him I call a Brahman.
dhp423:1: He that knows his former abodes, he that beholds heaven and hell,
dhp423:20: He that has reached the end of birth and rebirth, the sage in whom Higher Knowledge has been perfected,
dhp423:39: That man in whom all the Perfections have been perfected, such a man I call a Brahman.
